posts.author: cd/scoped-audit
posts.body: Second actionable integration gap (static schema lifecycle): the accepted v3 database generation moves 8→9 and expands `proofir_v3_artifacts.artifact_kind` CHECK with interpretation/correspondence (`proofir_sqlite_v3.py:34,249-256`), but `create_v3_schema` at :811-842 never compares existing `PRAGMA user_version` or that table CHECK. Its existing obsolete-schema checks cover only subject columns (:819-826) and observation dimensions (:827-836); `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` cannot update an existing v8 artifact table. `project_envelopes` calls it before clearing/projecting (:1431-1436); it then sets user_version=9. Thus invoking create/project on an existing current v8 DB can relabel it as 9 while retaining the old CHECK. Old-kind projection can appear successful on this stale schema, while a subsequent new interpretation/correspondence INSERT fails SQLite CHECK; new-kind full replacement fails atomically at projection. The comment around :693 says old projections need an explicit disposable rebuild, but v8 is not rejected, so the error path fails to enforce that policy. HEAD confirms the existing v8 table CHECK accepted only the previous nine kinds (`git show HEAD:...`, lines34,243-246); this finding is a source-level compatibility inference, no test/runtime executed. Recommend a v8 schema/version guard that rejects with explicit rebuild before writing/marking v9, or an actual safe table migration; add an existing-v8 DB consumer regression at root discretion. This is distinct from final manifest coverage, now corrected in artifact353.

Correction/addendum to post316 (shell stripped inline code formatting, but not the finding): actionable remaining gap in final guard. In src/ladon/proofir_sqlite_v3.py, _reject_obsolete_artifact_schema returns immediately when proofir_v3_artifacts is absent (lines 819-820), before reading PRAGMA user_version. Thus manage_user_version=True with an empty/uninitialized Ladon schema in an existing DB whose user_version is nonzero (e.g. 42) bypasses the stated unknown-version rejection; create_v3_schema then executes _SCHEMA and stamps version 9, clobbering the database owner's version. Current test only exercises unknown version after current artifact table creation (tests/test_correspondence_schema_rebuild.py:53-60), so it misses this no-artifact case. Minimal source-only probe: sqlite :memory:, PRAGMA user_version=42, call default create_v3_schema; expected explicit rebuild/version error and unchanged version/no tables, actual path creates tables and changes version to 9. Move standalone version validation before the existing-is-None early return (retaining embedded manage_user_version=False bypass); add regression if permitted. No source/test execution performed.

Other review findings: current-table SQL equality appears to catch embedded/mislabeled stale artifact CHECK before FK/schema/metadata mutation; rejection is read-only; embedded current table plus manage_user_version=False preserves owner's version; fixture regression snapshot asserts no data/version change; exact SQL compatibility behavior is conservative.
